overview: Deere's fiscal Q3 2026 net sales and revenues rose 5% to $12.608B, with equipment operations net sales up 6% to $10.999B at a 14.4% operating margin and net income of $1.379B, or $5.10 per diluted share. Dan Pooley, Manager, Investor Communications, raised FY2026 net income guidance to $4.75B-$5B and equipment operations cash flow to $5B-$5.5B. Brent Norwood, CFO, said 2026 represents the bottom of the ag equipment cycle, and Deanna Kovar said MY2027 planter and sprayer early orders are up mid-single digits.
keyTakeaways: Brent Norwood, CFO, said Deere continues to believe 2026 represents the bottom of the ag equipment cycle, with Deanna Kovar, President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf, expecting a measured recovery rather than a sharp rebound in 2027.

Kovar said MY2027 planter and sprayer early orders are up mid-single digits versus last year's completed programs, with See & Spray factory-installed orders doubling and 40% of planters taking the most advanced technologies.

Chris Seibert, Director of Investor Relations, said FY2026 direct tariff expense falls to about $1.1B from $1.2B excluding refunds, mainly on Section 232 changes cutting the rate on imported goods from roughly 25% to 15%.
Norwood said net tariffs will be a headwind in 2027, with a run rate closer to around $1B versus roughly $750M net this year.
Seibert said Construction & Forestry has four to five months of orders on hand versus the typical two to three, driven by infrastructure, data center starts and rental channels.
financialHighlights: Net sales and revenues were $12.608B, up 5%, with equipment operations net sales of $10.999B, up 6%, and a 14.4% operating margin.
Net income attributable to Deere was $1.379B, or $5.10 per diluted share, with $110M of incremental tariff refunds recognized in Q3 and $382M year to date.
Production & Precision Ag net sales fell 6% to $3.998B with a 13.2% operating margin, while Small Ag & Turf rose 12% to $3.383B at 18.4%.
Construction & Forestry net sales rose 18% to $3.618B at a 12.1% operating margin, with price up 8 points.
guidance: Pooley guided FY2026 net income to $4.75B-$5B and equipment operations operating cash flow to $5B-$5.5B, with Financial Services net income of $870M.

Pooley guided Production & Precision Ag net sales down approximately 10% with an 11%-12% margin, Small Ag & Turf up approximately 15% with a 14.5%-15.5% margin, and Construction & Forestry up approximately 20% with a 10.5%-11.5% margin.
Pooley guided U.S. and Canada large ag industry sales down 15%-20%, South America down 15%-20%, Europe approximately flat, and U.S. and Canada construction equipment up 5%-10%.

Norwood expects Q4 net sales for Production & Precision Ag and Construction & Forestry similar to Q3, with no refund benefit and margins for PPA and Small Ag & Turf a little lower on seasonally higher R&D and SA&G.
Seibert said direct tariff expense is approximately $1.1B excluding refunds, with no further refunds assumed in the outlook.

qa.question: With roughly $800M of net tariff impact this year, is net tariff impact a headwind, tailwind or neutral for 2027?
qa.answer: Norwood said net tariffs will be a headwind next year: about $1.1B of direct tariffs less $382M of refunds is roughly $750M net this year, and the 2027 run rate is closer to around $1B. He said there will be a bit of a step up in tariff expense versus this year.

qa.question: How could mix, including higher technology take rates, affect 2027 compared with the 2- to 3-point mix benefit discussed in prior years?
qa.answer: Seibert said it is too early to tell, especially in South America where things can turn quickly, citing input and commodity volatility, Black Sea disruptions and softness in the E.U. and Brazil. He said early order program signals will drive mix depending on how they wrap up.

qa.question: What regional variability is behind the early order program, and could mid-single-digit growth end up high single digits?
qa.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Ag & Turf, PPA, Sales and Marketing, Americas and Australia
qa.answer: Kovar said the programs are still open with a couple of weeks left on sprayers and a little longer on planters, and the U.S. is trending slightly better than Canada. She said time will tell whether mid-single digits turns more positive, citing See & Spray factory orders doubling and 40% of planters taking the most advanced technologies.
qa.read: Answered partially: would not call the final range.

qa.question: Why does C&F guidance imply roughly 50bp of positive price in Q4 versus 8% in Q3, and does Deere want to grow dealer rental?
qa.answer: Seibert said Q3 price of 8% was partly easy comps, since Q3 2025 had about 5% negative price from incentives, and Q4 has nothing outsized. Norwood said 30%-35% of earthmoving transactions start as a rental and dealer-owned fleets could boost inventory fill next year.
qa.read: Answered partially: did not reconcile the 50bp implied Q4 figure.

qa.question: What are the pricing expectations for 2027 given the early order program is up mid-single digits?
qa.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Ag & Turf, PPA, Sales and Marketing, Americas and Australia
qa.answer: Kovar said early order program pricing was rolled out several months ago and the focus is covering inflation into 2027. Seibert said PPA and C&F are each modestly underproducing in 2026 by a couple of percentage points.

qa.question: Could the 2028 EU CAP policy change pull demand forward into 2027, and is there a directional forecast for Europe in 2027?
qa.answer: Seibert said it is too early to tell, order books run four to five months out and Q1 orders are just starting. He gave no pull-forward view and no 2027 forecast.

whatChanged.toneShift: The prior call held the baseline that 2026 is the bottom with 'some level of recovery in 2027' and said it was very early on early orders; this call cites early orders up mid-single digits and frames 2027 as 'a measured recovery rather than a sharp rebound'.
